response: Kant's second critique, the "Critique of Practical Reason," focuses on the principles of morality and the nature of practical reason. It argues that the moral law is derived from pure reason and is universally applicable. Kant introduces the concept of the categorical imperative, which is the foundation of all moral obligations. He also discusses the idea of the highest good, which is the ultimate aim of practical reason. The critique establishes the autonomy of the will and the importance of treating humanity as an end in itself.
